messages:
Marta: Quick copy review for the new telemetry consent banner in the Console. Current text: 'Help us improve by sending anonymous telemetry.' Support wants clearer opt-in language and a less technical CTA. Screenshot in Figma.
Ethan: Agree. 'Telemetry' is jargon for many customers. Suggest 'usage data' or 'product analytics'. Also we need to be explicit about what is collected: 'anonymous usage data (no code or secrets)'.
Priya: Legal asks we avoid 'anonymous' alone; better to say 'aggregated, non-identifying usage data'. Also we should include a link to the privacy details.
Sam: For accessibility, banner needs keyboard-focusable controls and clear aria-labels. The primary action should be a toggle or button? If it's a one-time consent, a CTA 'Allow usage data' vs 'Opt in' — which is clearer?
Marta: I prefer 'Allow usage data' verb-first. 'Opt in' is fine but slightly terse. We also should provide a secondary CTA 'Manage settings' that opens the privacy panel.
Ethan: Copy variants:
1) Short / product-friendly: 'Help us improve Redwood Inference. Allow aggregated, non-identifying usage data.' CTA: 'Allow usage data' Secondary: 'Manage settings'
2) Explicit legal-friendly: 'Allow Redwood to collect aggregated, non-identifying usage data to improve product performance. No request bodies or secrets are collected.' CTA: 'Allow collection' Secondary: 'Privacy details'
3) Minimal: 'Send anonymous usage data to help improve product.' CTA: 'Allow' Secondary: 'No thanks'
Priya: I prefer variant 2 for enterprise defaults. It clearly states boundaries. But keep main CTA text shorter: 'Allow collection' is OK. Also add an opt-out link 'Change later' to reassure users.
Sam: Accessibility notes:
- Use role="region" with aria-label='Telemetry consent' so SR users can jump to it
- Make primary CTA a real <button> not a link, and announce the result with aria-live polite when toggled
- If we use a toggle, ensure aria-checked is present and the label reads state: 'Usage data collection on'/'off'
Marta: UX decision question: show banner to all users or only new accounts? Product wants to show to all until dismissed. Legal prefers showing it on first login with clear opt-out. Maybe show persistently for 7 days then collapse to a link in settings.
Ethan: Implementation note: keep the default OFF for regions with strict privacy laws, and surface a per-deployment config for Private customers to disable the banner. We'll need a server flag.
Priya: Microcopy tweaks: avoid 'Help us' as it sounds like begging. Use 'Help improve Redwood Inference' or 'Improve Redwood Inference' instead. Also use 'we collect' not 'we send' for clarity.
Marta: Final proposed strings (shortlist):
A) Title-less banner text: 'Allow Redwood to collect aggregated, non-identifying usage data to improve product performance. No request bodies or secrets are collected.' CTA primary: 'Allow collection' Secondary: 'Privacy details'
B) Short form for small screens: 'Allow aggregated usage data to help improve the product.' CTA: 'Allow' Link: 'Privacy'
C) Friendly form: 'Help us make Redwood better. Share aggregated, non-identifying usage data.' CTA: 'Allow usage data' Secondary: 'Manage settings'
Sam: For screen readers, append hidden text after the CTA result: 'You have allowed usage data collection. You can change this in Settings > Privacy.' Announce on change with aria-live.
Priya: Legal note: include a link to the DPA or privacy page for enterprise customers and ensure translations of 'non-identifying' are validated. Also avoid 'anonymous' as sole descriptor.
Marta: Action items:
- @Ethan: implement banner component with aria-live update and server-side flag for Private deployments (owner).
- @Priya: finalize legal-approved copy and privacy links (owner).
- @Sam: add a11y QA checklist to the PR and verify focus behaviors.
- @design-bot: create a tracking task for the banner rollout and include copy variants for small screens.
design-bot: Task created: PRIV-UI-5 "Telemetry consent banner copy + a11y" Assigned: Ethan, Priya Due: 2024-07-30
Priya: I'll post the final approved strings here once legal signs off.
Marta: Thanks team 44d
